subject: Custom uptime covenant and order-form excerpt for Meridian Health — SOC2 enclave routing
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:08:00Z
Subject: Notes from Meridian call — uptime covenant ask and SOC2 enclave requirement

Team,

Quick recap from this morning's 30-min call with Samantha (Meridian) and John (procurement). High-level: Meridian is comfortable with Redwood’s standard MSA but needs a narrowly scoped uptime covenant in the order form that: 1) defines a tighter P95 latency target for API calls to their dedicated private deployment, 2) documents regional failover sequencing, and 3) includes a SOC2 "enclave" routing requirement for queries touching PHI (they'll provide a matrix).

Action items I promised:
- Draft an order-form uptime exhibit excerpt they can show legal (they want redline-friendly language).
- Flag any operational limits (burst protection, per-customer concurrency) that would prevent meeting a 95% P95 target at 100 rps sustained.
- Confirm evidence and telemetry (they asked for 90 days of request-level latency histograms and per-route token-level cost breakdowns).

Attachments they sent: SOC2_enclave_matrix.xlsx (we've uploaded to the shared drive).

Can Kimberly and Lauren take first pass on a concise order-form excerpt (one page preferred) and a short runbook blurb describing routing for the SOC2 enclave? They want something to include with procurement by EOD Tuesday (Meridian is on a tight procurement window).

Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

---

(Attachment stub: SOC2_enclave_matrix.xlsx — spreadsheet mapping data types to routing tier)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@meridianhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: John Perez <john.perez@meridianhealth.com>, Meridian Procurement <procurement@meridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Notes from Meridian call — uptime covenant ask and SOC2 enclave requirement

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick recap and for taking ownership. To reiterate our priorities from legal and procurement:

- We need a short, explicit exhibit in the order form that references uptime (monthly availability) and a P95 API latency target for the dedicated environment our team will run in our VPC.
- For PHI-scoped traffic, calls must route to an infra "enclave" that is auditable and backed by SOC2 artifacts; the attached matrix shows which endpoints and payloads are considered PHI.
- Evidence: procurement requests a sample telemetry export (24–72 hour slice) and a description of the retention window and access controls for audit logs.

Time is sensitive — we plan to present your language to our legal lead on Wednesday morning. If you can provide a redlineable doc and confirm whether Redwood can commit to a regional failover sequence (primary region -> secondary region -> degraded-mode with scaled credits), that will help us move quickly.

Also: what would an availability credit schedule look like if there is a partial degradation (e.g., regional latency spikes vs full region outage)? We don't need the final schedule today but a proposed structure would be helpful.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Vendor Risk & Compliance | Meridian Health
samantha.lee@meridianhealth.com
(Attachment: SOC2_enclave_matrix.xlsx — courtesy copy)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@meridianhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:35:00Z
Subject: Proposed order-form uptime excerpt + enclave routing blurb (draft)

Samantha — attaching a concise draft excerpt below (we've kept it intentionally narrow so it can live inside the order form). Please let us know any legal redline suggestions.

--- BEGIN DRAFT EXCERPT ---
Order Form Exhibit: Availability and Enclave Routing
1) Availability. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Redwood Inference API available to Customer in the provisioned Dedicated environment at a monthly availability of 99.90% (the "Availability Target"). Availability is measured as the percentage of successful API request time periods within a calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance windows of at least 24 hours’ notice and agreed emergency maintenance.

2) Latency Commitment. For production API endpoints specified in this Order Form, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain a P95 per-request server-side latency <= 250ms for payloads under 2k tokens at steady-state traffic up to 100 requests/second per-region. Latency commitments exclude periods identified as force majeure, Customer-originated DDoS, or Customer-misconfigured routing.

3) Enclave Routing for PHI. Requests matching the Customer-provided PHI matrix will be routed to the Customer’s SOC2-compliant enclave within the specified region. Redwood will provide access logs and routing attestations for those requests for a rolling 90-day window.

4) Regional Failover Sequence. Redwood will perform regional failover as follows: primary region -> secondary region (automatic within configured failover window) -> degraded mode with scaled credits (manual escalation). Specific failover timing and crediting thresholds will be included in the runbook appendix.

5) Credits. In the event Redwood fails to meet the Availability Target, Customer will be eligible for service credits per the credit schedule attached to this Order Form. The credit schedule distinguishes between (a) partial degradations (e.g., P95 latency breach not impacting majority of requests) and (b) full regional outages.
--- END DRAFT EXCERPT ---

Attachments sent: MSA_v2_redline.pdf (redlines we've started), orderform_uptime_exhibit.docx (editable draft), and a one-page runbook excerpt describing the enclave routing and telemetry exports.

Regarding the telemetry slice: we can provide a 72-hour sample next-day (request-level histograms, error breakdowns, per-route P95). Retention: access logs and routing attestations are retained for 90 days by default; longer retention is available as an add-on.

A couple of notes on limits: maintaining 250ms P95 at sustained 100 rps requires the dedicated pool sizing we discussed in the call; without the requested reserved capacity we would need to flag this as best-effort with surge throttling. If Meridian wants guaranteed throughput we should reflect a capacity commitment in the order form (we included optional language in the draft).

K.
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

(Attachment stubs: orderform_uptime_exhibit.docx, MSA_v2_redline.pdf, runbook_enclave_excerpt.txt)

> On Nov 21, 2026, at 09:08, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Quick recap from this morning's 30-min call with Samantha (Meridian) and John (procurement). High-level: Meridian is comfortable with Redwood’s standard MSA but needs a narrowly scoped uptime covenant...

From: John Perez <john.perez@meridianhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Meridian Procurement <procurement@meridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposed order-form uptime excerpt + enclave routing blurb (draft)

Kimberly, Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the succinct draft. Procurement/legal reviewed this morning and asked for two small clarifications before we proceed to signature:

1) Please expand the "Availability" measurement sentence to explicitly state the metric ("successful request count divided by total request attempts, per calendar month") so our SLA team can map it to monitoring alerts.
2) For the credit schedule, supply an example calculation for a partial degradation (e.g., when P95 breaches to 350ms for a single region for 4 hours during business hours). An example line-item helps our finance team estimate exposure.

If you can push an updated doc with those two clarifications we can present to legal for a final sign-off. Also, when you send the telemetry slice please include a README describing field names (timestamp, route, latency_ms_p95, error_rate, request_count).

We prefer DocuSign for the order form — please route to procurement@meridianhealth.com when ready.

John Perez
Senior Manager, Procurement | Meridian Health
john.perez@meridianhealth.com

(Next steps: Redwood to upload updated orderform_uptime_exhibit.docx with the two clarifications and push a 72-hour telemetry sample + README to the shared drive. DocuSign route to procurement@meridianhealth.com pending final sign-off.)
